text:
Nick Suzuki won the Selke last season, and the quiet part of his game is still the best part. Evolving-Hockey had him fourth among all forwards in wins above replacement in 2025-26, against the other team's best players every night. This season he has 20 points in 18 games at nearly 21 minutes a night, and Montreal takes 54% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, five points better than without him (expected goals measure the quality of chances).

Some of the production has help: Montreal has scored about 4.3 more goals than its chances with him on the ice, so the point pace may cool even if his play doesn't. Our range has him around 85 points. The power play is the sore spot. He said it was "definitely not broken," and by the end of that night, as Sportsnet's Eric Engels wrote, it needed fixing. Dylan Larkin's arrival gives Montreal another top center, and how Martin St-Louis uses the two of them is the thing to watch.
